files.document_title: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection permit application PAD320011 (HCPP Pipeline), Pennsylvania Groundwater Information System water well map, Figure 1, sheet 1A of 5, drawn by Civil and Environmental Consultants, May 28, 2026
files.what_it_shows: Aerial photo sheet at 1 inch to 500 feet with the proposed pipeline as an orange line, the proposed limit of disturbance in red and a 500 foot pipeline buffer in pink. The five sheets (1A to 1E) run from the Homer City Generating Station end south to the Campbells Mill Road end, and each overlaps the next.

files.document_title: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection fact sheet for permit application PAD320011, HCPP Pipeline, May 5, 2026, page 1 map
files.what_it_shows: An overview aerial map with the route in red and soil unit labels. Its labels do not match the fact sheet text: it shows Bell Point Road, Larimer Road, Cecil Street, Salina Extension Road, a Bell Point 6 well pad and a proposed withdrawal location on the Kiskiminetas River, and none of the roads the text says the gas pipeline crosses. It may be a different line, probably a water supply line, so it is not used as the route for this row.

searched: The two documents attached to the oilandgaswatch record: a Pennsylvania Bulletin page with the public hearing notice for permit PAD320011 and the full Bulletin issue; neither has a map
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection fact sheet for PAD320011 and the Homer City portal folder tree on files.dep.state.pa.us (Application, Permit and Review folders)

The application folder: a 344 MB main application (skipped as too large), a 49 MB revised application (not downloaded), a wildlife determination letter with no map, and the water well map figure, which is the map used
The comment response document, searched for a route description
notes: The best map is the five-sheet water well map in the permit application folder, drawn on aerial photos with the proposed pipeline in orange. It covers the whole route in five overlapping sheets, so a georeferencer would work from the sheets together. The text of the Department's fact sheet describes the route: it starts at a meter and regulation facility in Burrell Township about 1.6 miles northwest of the State Route 119 and State Route 22 intersection, off Campbells Mill Road, runs north about 5.8 miles and ends at the Homer City Generating Station in Center Township, crossing Falling Run Road, McConnell Road, Blacklick Road, Dickey Road and Power Plant Road. The overview map on the fact sheet appears to show a different line (see its entry). The 49 MB revised application of March 9, 2026 and the 344 MB original application likely hold a project overview map and alignment sheets and could be read if a tighter fit is needed. url_verifier cannot read the water well map PDF because it is an image-only file, so it was read by rendering the pages.
